calls.head: Point-blank against perimeter
calls.body: Pittsburgh ranks 5th of 32 for shot quality, toward the point-blank end; Winnipeg ranks 30th, toward the perimeter end.
calls.call: Pittsburgh’s shots are more dangerous on average than Winnipeg’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, Pittsburgh had 1 goal per 14.3 shots and Winnipeg 1 goal per 16.2 shots. Coming in, Pittsburgh was at 1 goal per 15.1 shots and Winnipeg at 1 goal per 17.0 shots.

calls.head: Volume against patience
calls.body: Pittsburgh ranks 8th of 32 for shot volume, toward the relentless end; Winnipeg ranks 24th, toward the selective end.
calls.call: Pittsburgh takes more 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than Winnipeg.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Pittsburgh had 64.5 per 60 and Winnipeg 63.1 per 60. Coming in, Pittsburgh was at 59.3 per 60 and Winnipeg at 53.7 per 60.

PIT.head: We gave Pittsburgh a 66% chance, but Winnipeg had other ideas.

WPG.head: We gave Winnipeg a 34% chance, and Winnipeg proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Winnipeg shut down Pittsburgh’s power play
surprises.body: Pittsburgh’s power play created 2.0 expected goals per 60, against its usual 7.7 and a league average of 7.6. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Winnipeg shortened its bench
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s bottom-six forwards played 39% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against its usual 42% and a league average of 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 7 games.
